title: All Tables — Bolus + HRS Criteria Cohort
text:
Every table from Tables.Rmd (/Users/to909/Desktop/Tables), recomputed on the cohort restricted to bolus terlipressin initiation (terli_route_day0 == 1) AND at least one of criteria 1–4 met (HRS_Criteria == 1). Each table has a Download Excel link directly underneath; the same tables are also written as CSVs to Results/.
Conventions (identical to the originals): continuous variables are median [IQR] with Kruskal–Wallis tests (= Mann–Whitney for two groups); categorical variables are n (%) with chi-squared tests, or Fisher’s exact test where the original used it (adverse-event tables); Missing is the percentage of the cohort missing that variable; the Overall column is display-only — p-values compare the strata.

results_dir <- "/Users/to909/Desktop/Terlipressin projects/Request/Request 11:19:2026/Results"
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("tables", showWarnings = FALSE)

run_notes <- character(0)
note <- function(msg) {
  run_notes <<- c(run_notes, msg)
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Build one table exactly as Tables.Rmd did (tableone; showAllLevels, nonnormal
# = all continuous vars, Missing %), write it as CSV (Results/) and XLSX
# (docs/tables/, served by the site), and return it as a kable.
# - Variables not in the data, or entirely missing within the cohort, are
#   dropped and recorded in `run_notes`.
# - If the stratifier has fewer than 2 levels inside this cohort (e.g.
#   HRS_Criteria, terli_route_day0), the table falls back to an overall-only
#   column and that is recorded too.
make_table <- function(all_vars, data, strata, slug,
                       cat_vars = NULL, exact = NULL, caption = NULL,
                       family = slug) {
  all_vars <- unique(trimws(all_vars))

  not_in_data <- setdiff(all_vars, names(data))
  if (length(not_in_data) > 0) {
    note(paste0(family, ": not collected in the master dataset, dropped: ",
                paste(not_in_data, collapse = ", "), "."))
    all_vars <- intersect(all_vars, names(data))
  }

  all_na <- all_vars[sapply(data[all_vars], function(x) all(is.na(x)))]
  if (length(all_na) > 0) {
    note(paste0(family, ": entirely missing within this cohort, dropped: ",
                paste(all_na, collapse = ", "), "."))
    all_vars <- setdiff(all_vars, all_na)
  }

  cat_vars <- intersect(unique(trimws(cat_vars)), all_vars)
  exact <- intersect(unique(trimws(exact)), all_vars)
  numerical_vars <- setdiff(all_vars, cat_vars)

  strata_levels <- if (is.null(strata)) character(0) else unique(na.omit(as.character(data[[strata]])))
  use_strata <- !is.null(strata) && length(strata_levels) >= 2
  if (!is.null(strata) && !use_strata) {
    note(paste0(family, ": stratifier `", strata, "` has a single level in this cohort (all = ",
                paste(strata_levels, collapse = "/"), ") - overall column only, no tests."))
  }

  if (use_strata) {
    T1 <- tableone::CreateTableOne(
      vars = all_vars, strata = strata, data = data,
      factorVars = cat_vars, addOverall = TRUE, includeNA = FALSE
    )
  } else {
    T1 <- tableone::CreateTableOne(
      vars = all_vars, data = data,
      factorVars = cat_vars, includeNA = FALSE
    )
  }

  T1_print <- print(
    T1,
    showAllLevels = TRUE,
    exact         = if (use_strata) exact else NULL,
    nonnormal     = numerical_vars,
    missing       = TRUE,
    quote         = FALSE,
    noSpaces      = TRUE,
    printToggle   = FALSE
  )

  # The original CSVs leave the p-value blank (not "NA") for degenerate
  # single-level variables; match that.
  if ("p" %in% colnames(T1_print)) {
    p_na <- is.na(T1_print[, "p"]) | T1_print[, "p"] == "NA"
    T1_print[p_na, "p"] <- ""
  }

  write.csv(T1_print, file = file.path(results_dir, paste0(slug, ".csv")), row.names = TRUE)
  write_xlsx(
    data.frame(Variable = rownames(T1_print), T1_print,
               row.names = NULL, check.names = FALSE),
    file.path("tables", paste0(slug, ".xlsx"))
  )

  knitr::kable(T1_print, caption = caption)
}

# Numeric coercions first (before any factor conversion)
cohort <- cohort %>%
  mutate(
    mido_maxdose_before_terli = as.numeric(mido_maxdose_before_terli),

  mutate(across(any_of(num_hrs_clinical_course_variables), as.numeric)) %>%
  # Factor conversions (as in Tables.Rmd; make_table also passes factorVars)
  mutate(across(any_of(unique(c(
    categorical_vars, cat_followup_variables,
    cat_hospitalization_course_variables, cat_hrs_clinical_course_variables

Patient dies day 50, transplanted day 40: time = 40, status = 2 (transplant came first)

title: Request 11/19/2026 — All Tables, Bolus + HRS Criteria Cohort
section: What changed vs. the original Tables.Rmd output
text:
What changed vs. the original Tables.Rmd output

Cohort restriction — every table is computed on the bolus + HRS-criteria cohort (N = 118) instead of the full registry.
Data source — tables are built from the cleaned master dataset via the shared pipeline (per project convention), not by re-merging the raw site CSVs from Dropbox as Tables.Rmd does.
Collapsed stratifiers — “AE by HRS_Criteria” and “AE by terli_route_day0” are constant in this cohort by definition, so they are replaced by a single overall AE table.
One fixed cohort for every table — the original applied drop_na(HRS_reversal_new, hrs_responders) midway through the document (see issue 2 below); here the cohort never changes, and rows missing a given stratifier are excluded only from that table (standard tableone behavior).
Downloads — every table is downloadable as Excel from the Analysis page; CSVs are written to Results/.

title: Request 11/19/2026 — All Tables, Bolus + HRS Criteria Cohort
text:
Validation against the original tables
As a fidelity check, the engine used here was pointed at the full registry (no cohort filter) and compared cell-by-cell against the most recent original outputs (Jan 2026): table1_check_0128_HRS_criteria_meld.csv, table_followup_0128…, table_hospitalization_0128…, table_hrs_clinical_0128…, and ae by HRS_criteria_meld 2026.csv. All five tables reproduce exactly — 0 differing cells of 4,536 — after matching two cosmetic conventions: locale-dependent sorting of free-text levels (en_US.UTF-8 collation) and blank-vs-NA p-value formatting for degenerate single-level variables. The only intended difference in the tables published here is the cohort restriction.

title: Request 11/19/2026 — All Tables, Bolus + HRS Criteria Cohort
section: Issues found in Tables.Rmd while porting
text:
Issues found in Tables.Rmd while porting

INU site labeled as MCM (Tables.Rmd line 63) — the INU file is read with id = paste0("mcm_", row_number()), so INU rows share the “mcm_” prefix with Mayo Clinic MCM rows. The REDCap subjectid used for merges is unaffected (verified unique in the master dataset), so published tables were not affected, but the id field is wrong in Tables.Rmd.
Mid-document cohort change (line 2029) — final_master <- final_master %>% drop_na(HRS_reversal_new, hrs_responders) runs before the KM section, and every table generated after it (all “ae by …” CSVs, the MAP table, and the 2026 “0128” CSVs) inherits that filter. Verified harmless in the current data: neither variable has missing values in the final dataset, so zero rows were dropped (all original CSVs show n = 243) — but it is a latent hazard if the response derivation ever changes. This rebuild uses one fixed cohort for every table instead.
Wrong variable list in two HTML tables (lines 1990 and 2012) — the “numeric hospitalization course” table1() formulas were built from num_hrs_clinical_course_variables, so those HTML tables showed HRS-clinical variables instead of hospitalization variables. The CSV outputs were not affected.
Unassigned mutate in “ae by criteria_2” (line 2323) — final_master %>% mutate(criteria_2 = if_else(admit_meld_3_raw >= 35, …)) is never assigned; had it been, it would have overwritten the ACLF-based criteria_2 with a MELD flag. The table actually stratified by the original ACLF-based criteria_2, which is what this rebuild does explicitly.
Trailing-space variable name (line 1323) — "mido_maxdose_before_terli " (with a trailing space) duplicates the correctly spelled entry and was silently dropped by tableone every run. Removed here.
List duplicates / stray entries — time_to_death_90days listed twice; time_to_death_status in both the numeric and categorical lists (treated as categorical); dc_lt_90days twice in the follow-up categorical list; tips_1yr_days named in the categorical list but never collected. Deduplicated here; no effect on values.
Follow-up availability flags not in the master dataset — dc_30scr_notavailable, dc_60scr_notavailable, dc_90scr_notavailable, dc_90scr_notavailable_lt, last_encounter_1yr, scr_available_1yr are not columns in the master dataset (REDCap exports availability as *___999 checkboxes). The original skipped them silently; here they are recorded in the Run notes on the Analysis page.
MAP “0” readings — MAP values recorded as 0 (“not measured” placeholders) are averaged into the daily means in the MAP table (shared-pipeline bug S3). Kept identical to the original for comparability and flagged on the Analysis page.

Dynamic notes from the actual run (variables dropped per table family, collapsed stratifiers) are printed in the Run notes section at the bottom of the Analysis page.
